ops.title: M8 crashpad ownership contract: launch-owned nonce evidence, preserve unowned matches (root review of 921e0d4)
ops.body:
Root's final delta review of PR #3 head 921e0d4 (2026-09-30, report `recovery-20260930/cookiesync-m8-root-review.md`, bus #280/#283) returned CHANGES_REQUESTED on M8 only: `internal/bridge/crashpad_linux.go` adopted any /proc process whose argv carried `--database=<dataDir>/Crashpad` and pidfd-signaled it; the pidfd pins identity, not creation ownership, and `TestServesCrashpadDatabase` / `TestHandlerTrackerReapsOnlyItsSessionsHandlers` positively asserted that an arbitrary `/bin/sh` with the matching argument is adopted and killed. M7 (daemonkit v0.32.2 + real Program) was accepted.

Contract adopted (bus #292): (1) each Linux bridge launch generates a 16-byte crypto/rand nonce exported only through the environment as `COOKIESYNC_BRIDGE_LAUNCH=<nonce>`, never argv; crashpad's double-fork `execv` inherits the browser environ so the real handler carries it. (2) Adoption requires the session `--database=` argv match AND the exact nonce in `/proc/<pid>/environ`; the pidfd is opened before the evidence read (a pid reused between read and open would pin the wrong process; the reverse only pins a dead one); (pid, pidfd, starttime, evidence) recorded before any signal. (3) A matching candidate without the nonce or with unreadable environ is preserved, never signaled; Close reaps owned handlers only and returns a cleanup refusal naming each preserved pid and database. No name/tag/group/UID sweep; Darwin bytes unchanged. (4) Tests invert the unrelated expectation (unowned double survives Close and is named in the refusal; nonce-carrying doubles get TERM/KILL); the real-Chrome smoke keeps its strict pre/post-Close gate and now also proves the handler inherits the nonce. Fallback if CI shows the handler does not inherit the environment: PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER ancestry on the helper, brought back to root, never a weaker gate. Built speculatively in an isolated worktree; lands on PR #3 only after root's ack.
